reasoning: Per guidelines, Owner category = 'Government/ಸರ್ಕಾರಿ' without Saguvali Chit automatically triggers HIGH risk (70+)
The contradiction between 'Government' ownership category and 'ಪಿತ್ರಾಜಿತ' (ancestral/inherited) acquisition raises serious doubts about the chain of title
Without a Saguvali Chit (land grant certificate), the occupant cannot legally transfer/sell the property, as title still vests with the Government
Any sale by Kulle Gowda bin Channa would be void/voidable and subject to resumption by Government
Absence of PTCL, court stay, and mutation provide some comfort but do not override the fundamental title defect
recommendations: Do NOT proceed with purchase until Saguvali Chit / Grant Certificate is produced and verified
Obtain certified copy of Mutation Register (MR) extracts and trace title from original grant
Verify with Tahsildar, Kanakapura, whether the land has been granted to the recorded occupant and under what Government Order
Check if the land falls under any PTCL/Inams Abolition/Land Reforms restrictions requiring prior Government permission for sale
Obtain Form 7A/7B and Record of Rights history for last 30 years
If granted land, verify the non-alienation period (usually 15 years) under Karnataka Land Grant Rules has expired
Insist on a 'No Objection Certificate' from the Deputy Commissioner before registration
Engage a local advocate to inspect village records (Pahani, Index of Lands, Tippani) at the Taluk office
llm_risk.summary: HIGH RISK property. Although there is no court stay, PTCL endorsement, or ongoing mutation, the RTC classifies the owner category as 'Government' with NO Saguvali Chit (grant certificate), meaning the title still legally vests with the State. The contradictory 'ancestral acquisition' entry further muddies the chain of title. Purchase is strongly inadvisable without producing the grant certificate and verifying alienation permissions from revenue authorities.
